Asylum is a form of legal protection available to people fleeing persecution in their home countries if they meet certain criteria. Under U.S. law , an asylum seeker who "arrives in" the U.S. is entitled to apply for asylum and generally cannot be removed from the country until their asylum application is processed. By a 6-3 vote, the high court ruled that federal law allows the government to stop asylum seekers from physically setting foot in the country, effectively keeping them from applying for asylum. Two major cases were decided in early June, ahead of the court's final sprint to the end of the term, which ended on June 30: One essentially gutted what remained of the landmark 1965 Voting Rights Act, prompting Republicans in a number of Southern states to redraw congressional maps to diminish or eliminate majority-Black districts that have elected Black members of Congress. Poaching, trafficking, insurgencies and traditional medicine all threaten the central African primates, but a rehabilitation centre offers a haven in Cameroon Supported by About this content Words and photographs by Marta Meinardi Sun 15 Nov 2026 07.00 EST Last modified on Tue 17 Nov 2026 06.44 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Dr Christian Atonfack checks the vital signs of a chimpanzee that has just been sedated to undergo a dental procedure. E very morning in central Cameroon , the primatologist Sheri Speede wakes to a daunting task. At the Sanaga-Yong sanctuary, which she founded in 1999, there are 75 chimpanzees to feed four times a day and monitor for physical or behavioural issues. Of those, more than 30 need to be given routine birth-control medications, four are babies requiring round-the-clock care, and two are rowdy teenagers currently being integrated into new social groups. pages.text: Survey and Census History Survey and Census History Skip Navigation Within Survey and Census History Survey and Census History As the United States grew, the nation's interests became more complex. People and policy planners needed a more detailed idea of the economic and demographic characteristics of America so that they could make decisions and plan for the future. Because of this, the census expanded over time from a simple headcount in 1790 (which only classified Americans by age, sex, and race), to over 200 different surveys today. U.S. Census Bureau programs can be split into two broad categories: demographic and economic. The number of inquiries under each of these categories has expanded over time, gaining accuracy even as they also grow increasingly detailed. November 20, 1967 - President Lyndon B. Johnson announces that the census population clock reached the 200 million mark. In 1810, the census was expanded to obtain, for the first time, information on manufacturing and manufactured products. After a hiatus in 1830, the economic portion of the census returned in 1840, with added questions on agriculture, mining, and fisheries. The 1850 census also was the first demographic census to collect social data, including questions on taxation, churches, pauperism and crime. The amount of information collected would only increase in the following decades. With the creation of a permanent Census Bureau in 1902, there was an opportunity to expand the survey-taking role of the Census Bureau beyond the decennial demographic and economic censuses. Terrorists and criminals often conduct specific activities as they plan a bombing attack. These activities can include, but are not limited to, eliciting information, testing or probing of security, and observation/surveillance. Susquehanna National Heritage Area Quick Facts Location: Lancaster County and York County, PA Significance: Lancaster County, York County, and the Susquehanna River served as an early gateway to America’s frontier. The Susquehanna River facilitated transportation and trade for indigenous people and later settlers. Serving as the temporary seat of the Continental Congress during the Revolutionary War, the town of York saw the approval of the Articles of Confederation. The region was at the center of 19th-century conflicts over slavery as a major route on the Underground Railroad, home to influential political figures such as James Buchanan and Thaddeus Stevens, and strategic location during the Civil War. The area is also known for its scenic beauty, rich agriculture, and culture of Amish communities and other Plain People. pages.text: Sustainable events | Corporate Environmental Responsibility | FAO Share Close Corporate Environmental Responsibility Sustainable events Events often require significant resources—such as water, energy, food, and paper—within a short period of time. They can generate substantial amounts of waste and contribute to a carbon footprint, both through on site activities and through participant travel and accommodation. Making meetings and events more sustainable is therefore essential —not only to reduce environmental impact, but also to clearly demonstrate organizational values and commitments. A range of practical measures can be applied to significantly reduce the environmental footprint of in person events and support the delivery of climate neutral outcomes. The following measures can be applied to make events more sustainable: Reducing waste generated by meetings and conferences , particularly from printed materials and single use plastic water bottles; Improving energy efficiency through measures such as optimized lighting and smart control systems in meeting spaces; Using sustainable materials for furniture and fittings, including bamboo and other eco friendly alternatives; Promoting paper smart and plastic free conferences; Offering sustainable food and beverage options during coffee breaks and receptions; Raising awareness among participants and visitors to encourage active engagement in sustainability efforts; Offsetting carbon emissions associated with event organization and participation. FAO promotes SFA to help countries worldwide achieve Zero Hunger and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Find out more about FAO’s vision for Sustainable Food and Agriculture. Why are food and agriculture systems under threat today? Food and agriculture production systems worldwide are facing unprecedented challenges from an increasing demand for food for a growing population, rising hunger and malnutrition, adverse climate change effects, overexploitation of natural resources, loss of biodiversity, and food loss and waste. These challenges can undermine the world’s capacity to meet its food needs now and in the future. In other words, fewer people have adequate access to enough nutritious food. pages.text: Sustainable procurement | Corporate Environmental Responsibility | FAO Share Close Corporate Environmental Responsibility Sustainable procurement As an international organization with a global mandate, FAO has a strong responsibility to deliver its activities in an environmentally responsible and sustainable way . Sustainable procurement plays a key role in achieving this goal. For FAO, sustainable procurement goes beyond obtaining the best value for money. It is a strategic lever for generating positive benefits for society and the economy as a whole. This approach often requires additional time, resources, and close collaboration across the supply chain, as it looks at the wider environmental and social impacts of procurement decisions. FAO’s procurement function actively supports the Organization’s Corporate Environmental Responsibility Policy. This includes promoting best practices that reduce FAO’s environmental footprint while improving operational efficiency . Wherever feasible and in the best interest of the Organization and its stakeholders, environmental criteria are integrated into procurement processes, ensuring sustainability is a standard consideration rather than an afterthought. A good example for sustainable procurement practices is the IT hardware Long Term Agreement where the supplier committed to managing all activities in line with FAO’s Corporate Environmental Responsibility Policy , including collection of obsolete IT equipment, its consequent recycling, upgrading and reuse or disposal, ensuring a more sustainable approach throughout service delivery.

View in English Always switch to English SVG: Skalierbare Vektorgrafiken Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) ist eine auf XML basierende Auszeichnungssprache zur Beschreibung zweidimensionaler Vektorgrafiken . SVG ist damit ein textbasierter, offener Webstandard zur Beschreibung von Bildern, die sich bei jeder Größe scharf darstellen lassen. SVG wurde speziell für die Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Webstandards entwickelt, darunter CSS , DOM , JavaScript und SMIL . Im Wesentlichen ist SVG für Grafiken das, was HTML für Text ist. SVG-Bilder und ihr zugehöriges Verhalten werden in XML -Textdateien definiert. Dadurch lassen sie sich durchsuchen, indexieren, mit Skripten bearbeiten und komprimieren. Außerdem können sie mit jedem Texteditor oder mit Zeichenprogrammen erstellt und bearbeitet werden. Im Gegensatz zu klassischen Bitmap-Bildformaten wie JPEG oder PNG lassen sich Vektorgrafiken im SVG-Format ohne Qualitätsverlust in jeder Größe darstellen. Sie können außerdem einfach lokalisiert werden, indem der enthaltene Text geändert wird – ein Grafikeditor ist dafür nicht erforderlich. Mit geeigneten Bibliotheken lassen sich SVG-Dateien sogar dynamisch lokalisieren. SVG wird seit 1999 vom World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) entwickelt. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Swainson’s Hawks: a remarkable return to California’s Central Valley Oct 19, 2026 Swainson’s Hawks are medium-to-large raptors renowned for their elegant flight and extraordinary migratory journeys. Each year, these hawks travel thousands of miles between their breeding grounds in the western United States and Canada and their wintering sites in Central and South America. California’s Central Valley is especially critical to their life cycle, with 95 percent of the state’s Swainson’s Hawks nesting there. Upon arrival in the Central Valley, Swainson’s Hawks select nest sites near grasslands or agricultural fields, which offer abundant prey and shelter. During the breeding season, their diet consists mainly of rodents, rabbits, reptiles, and small birds, which are essential for raising their young. Outside the breeding season, they adapt by feeding primarily on insects such as grasshoppers, demonstrating remarkable versatility. Overview The "swarmvtab" virtual table allows the user to query a large number of tables (hereafter "component" tables) with similar schemas but distinct ranges of rowid values as if they were a single database table. The tables may be (and usually are) located in different databases. Swarmvtab tables are read-only. Component tables must not be declared WITHOUT ROWID, and must all have the same schema, but may have different names within their databases. In this context, "the same schema" means that: All component tables must have the same set of columns, in the same order. The types and default collation sequences attached to each column must be the same for all component tables. All component tables must have the same PRIMARY KEY declaration (if any). A swarmvtab table has the same schema as each of its component tables. A swarmvtab virtual table is created as follows: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE temp.<name> USING swarmvtab(<sql-statement>); Swarmvtab virtual tables must be created in the temp schema. A single annual payment from the Bibsam Consortium, covered by four national funders, will defray all publishing fees for all Bibsam participating institutions , including universities, public agencies and research institutes. Under this collaborative agreement, participating universities and research centers are empowered to facilitate their affiliated researchers in publishing an unlimited number of peer-reviewed articles across all Frontiers journals and Frontiers' partner journals. Researchers at those institutions can now publish an unlimited number of peer-reviewed articles in all Frontiers journals and partner society journals without charge. The agreement, which runs in a year-long pilot through 2024, is evidence of growing market appetite for simplicity, transparency, and frictionless publishing. pages.text: Switch-hitters getting noticed at MLB Breakthrough Series Skip to Content VERO BEACH, Fla. -- Most hitters spend years trying to perfect one swing. Deniel Gonzalez and Chris Woodson Jr. are working on two. Learning two swings requires years of repetition and countless patience. But the ability to hit from both sides of the plate can create advantages against pitchers, help in key situations and provide scouts with another reason to take notice. Those benefits are what drew both players to switch-hitting, a unique skill they brought to the Breakthrough Series at the Jackie Robinson Training Complex in Vero Beach. “The advantage is that I can get noticed more, in a way,” Gonzalez said. “Because obviously, not too many people hit on both sides, and it's just easier for at-bats in a game. … I thought this is a great [opportunity] to get your name out there.” One advantage comes when a left-handed hitter faces a right-handed pitcher and sees a release point farther away, giving him a fraction of a second longer to track the ball. It can also help in situational baseball, making it easier to move runners. Gonzalez started switch-hitting when he found out his dad, who played college ball at Queens College and Monroe College, was a switch-hitter. Symptoms and Care of RSV Feb. 20, 2026 What to know Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms. Most RSV infections go away on their own. RSV can be serious for babies, some young children, and adults who are older or have certain risk factors. Most RSV symptoms can be managed with over-the-counter medications. Overview People infected with RSV usually show symptoms within 4 to 6 days after getting infected. Symptoms of RSV infection usually include: Runny nose Congestion Decrease in appetite Coughing Sneezing Fever Wheezing These symptoms usually appear in stages and not all at once. In very young infants with RSV, their only symptoms may be irritability, decreased activity, and breathing difficulties. RSV can worsen underlying lung conditions like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or asthma. People with RSV infection and COPD or asthma may need treatment for asthma attacks or COPD flare-ups. When to seek emergency care Call your healthcare professional if you or your child are having difficulty breathing, not drinking enough fluids, or experiencing worsening symptoms. GitHub: https://github.com/nj-yzf/josm-BetterIME 问题背景 使用中文输入法编辑 OpenStreetMap 时，JOSM 的快捷键（如 S 选择、A 添加节点、W 提高路径精度等）经常被输入法拦截，导致快捷键失效。每次都要手动切换输入法，非常影响编辑效率。 为此我开发了 BetterIME 插件，让 JOSM 根据当前操作场景自动控制输入法状态。 功能介绍 插件将输入法控制分为三种场景： 自动切换至中文输入法： - 编辑 name、name:zh、name:zh-Hans、name:zh-Hant、alt_name、operator 标签时 - 打开 F3「搜索预设组合」对话框时 默认英文，可手动切换： - 其他文本输入框（如 Ctrl+F 查找、其他标签编辑等） 禁用输入法（快捷键正常工作）： - 地图视图、工具栏等非文本组件，Shift/Ctrl+Space 也无法意外切换至中文 此外，插件还释放了 Ctrl+Space 快捷键（JOSM 默认绑定为「搜索菜单项」），让它回归系统输入法切换功能。 首选项设置 通过 编辑 → 首选项 (F12) 打开 BetterIME 设置页，可以： 启用/禁用自动输入法切换（总开关） 启用/禁用 F3 搜索预设对话框中的中文输入法 启用/禁用基于标签键的自动检测 自定义触发中文输入法的标签键列表（支持添加、删除、重置） 所有设置即时生效，无需重启 JOSM。 安装方式 方式一：JOSM 内置插件管理器 1. 打开 编辑 → 首选项 → 插件 2. 搜索 BetterIME 3. 勾选启用，重启 JOSM 方式二：手动安装 1. 从 GitHub Releases 页面下载 BetterIME.jar： https://github.com/nj-yzf/josm-BetterIME/releases 2. 将 JAR 文件复制到 JOSM 插件目录（Windows: %APPDATA%\JOSM\plugins\） 3. 在 编辑 → 首选项 → 插件 中勾选启用，重启 JOSM 兼容性 JOSM 19555 及以上版本 Java 11 及以上 目前仅在 Windows 上测试过，macOS 和 Linux 上的输入法框架不同，可能无法正常工作，欢迎反馈测试结果 反馈 如果遇到问题或有功能建议，欢迎在 GitHub 提交 Issue： https://github.com/nj-yzf/josm-BetterIME/issues 许可证：GPL-2.0-or-later（与 JOSM 一致） Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.text: T. rex had lips, upending its enduring pop culture image | National Geographic Premium SCIENCE ​ T. rex had lips, upending its enduring pop culture image Whether carnivorous dinosaurs had lips has long been the stuff of paleo-debate. A new study finds evidence that flesh covered the predators’ teeth. Tyrannosaurus rex and other carnivorous dinosaurs likely had soft tissue that covered their sharp teeth, as seen in this illustration. Lips would have kept their teeth moist and protected—and ready to attack prey. Illustration by Mark P. Witton By Riley Black Published March 30, 2023 • 6 min read The fearsome jaws of Tyrannosaurus are famous. In museum halls, paleo art, and even feature films such as Jurassic Park , the Cretaceous carnivore has traditionally been depicted with banana-size fangs and a sinister grin. But paleontologists have now discovered that the living animal did not have a sharp-toothed smirk— T. rex , as well as many other carnivorous dinosaurs, had lips. Reported today in Science , a multi-institution team of paleontologists propose that carnivorous dinosaurs like T. rex and Allosaurus had fleshy lips covering their teeth, much as modern-day lizards do. The hypothesis will likely alter both the public image of dinosaurs as well as how paleontologists study the ways these terrible lizards fed. pages.description: The formidable Tyrannosaurus rex had nothing to fear—except possibly its own kind, gnawed fossil bones suggest.
pages.text: T. Rex Was a Cannibal, Bone Gashes Suggest | National Geographic Tooth gouges on this 65-million-year-old T. rex toe bone could have been made only by another T. rex. Diagram courtesy Nicholas Longrich, Yale University T. Rex Was a Cannibal, Bone Gashes Suggest Mighty predators may have attacked kin or scavenged corpses. By Brian Handwerk Published October 15, 2010 • 3 min read The formidable Tyrannosaurus rex likely had nothing to fear—except possibly its own kind, a new study suggests. Paleontologist Nick Longrich of Yale University was examining dinosaur bones found in Montana when he noticed large gouges in bones that had yet to be indentifiied. The gouges had to have been made by a large carnivore, he said, and when the mystery fossils were deposited 65 million years ago, T. rex was the only North American carnivore large and toothy enough to make such marks. But the seemingly routine find took a macabre turn when Longrich discovered one of the bitten bones belonged to a T. rex —making it apparent evidence of cannibalism. This toe bone "has giant theropod bite marks, and the only one there [at that time] was T. rex ," he said. "There was really no other conclusion I could come to." (Related: "Tiny T. rex Ancestors Achieved World Domination." ) Further analysis in several fossil collections turned up three more similarly bitten T. rex bones. Longrich and colleagues speculate the giant predators may have engaged in cannibalism with some regularity—but it's unknown whether the dinosaurs fought to the death or simply scavenged T. rex corpses. She explains why systematic manipulation is like the Hydra: cut off one head and two more grow back. Paper mills are evolving, and so must our response. From fabricated research papers to manipulated citations, fraudulent peer reviews, and authorship-for-sale schemes, systematic manipulation is becoming increasingly sophisticated. For editors, publishers, and research integrity professionals, recognizing the warning signs early and knowing how to respond have never been more important. On 5 November, I led a session as part of COPE's Publication Integrity Week 2026, exploring practical ways to identify and respond to organized manipulation of the publication process. Through real-world examples, audience polls, and discussions about policies and detection strategies, we explored what journals and publishers can do to strengthen their defenses, regardless of their size or resources. The discussion reinforced the importance of looking for signs of manipulation throughout the publication process and sharing what we learn across the research community. pages.text: Tag team: dual waterspouts appear in San Francisco Bay amid stormy weather | California | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Two waterspouts formed over the San Francisco Bay this past weekend, a rare weather occurrence California Tag team: dual waterspouts appear in San Francisco Bay amid stormy weather Phenomenon is not a common occurrence in the Bay area and inclement weather is expected to continue for few days Uwa Ede-Osifo Tue 17 Nov 2026 21.33 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 20.50 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A pair of waterspouts were recorded recently in the San Francisco Bay area, much to the delight and shock of several observers, as storms pummelled the region. Two waterspouts – vortexes of air and water mist, essentially tornadoes – cut a sheer streak into the sky, as they spiraled above the bay, according to social media footage capturing the weather phenomenon. While prevalent in the Great Lakes and the south-east Florida coast, waterspout sightings are not common for the Bay area, according to federal storm data. The National Weather Service (NWS) confirmed the waterspout occurrence in a special marine warning on Monday. Some waterspouts, dubbed “fair weather”, are weak, while others, typically tornadic waterspouts, can pose a risk to boaters and coastal areas if they travel on shore. pages.text: Tagging and Transcription for Chinese Heritage Records | National Archives Top Skip to main content Tagging and Transcription for Chinese Heritage Records From 1882 to 1943 the United States Government severely curtailed immigration from China to the United States, passing a series of laws whose result was the documentation of international movements of many Chinese nationals. Certain Federal agencies were particularly active in enforcing the exclusion laws, including the Customs Service, the Immigration and Naturalization Service (INS), which in 2003, became the United States Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS), and the U.S. District Courts. Many of the records created to implement the Chinese exclusion laws are now in the custody of the National Archives and have been digitized. The records are a major resource for the study of Chinese immigration and Chinese-American travel, trade, and social history from the late-19th to mid-20th century. Because many documents relate to individual immigrants, they are invaluable for the study of Chinese and Chinese-American family history. For more information about these records, please visit us online at https://www.archives.gov/research/chinese-americans Please help us tag, comment, and transcribe these records for greater access. Office de Tourisme de La Plagne Vallée By Isabel Conway Published September 12, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). A Paris railway station on a miserable, rainy January night feels worlds away from sunny alpine slopes and high-altitude soft powder. But vintage train carriages emblazoned with ‘Les Arcs’, ‘La Plagne’, ‘Tignes’, ‘Meribel’ and ‘Val d’Isere’ get my adrenaline flowing. At the belle époque-style Gare de Lyon, Guillaume de Marcillac, co-founder and CEO of Pegasus Trains, is greeting passengers about to board the sleeper train. He explains that by repurposing “elderly” train stock, his company offers travellers “a credible, low-impact alternative to flying or driving to their winter sport destination”. The train, chartered by UK tour operator Travelski for the 2025-26 winter season, is the first sleeper service to the Alps in nine years — and there are plans for it to run for winters to come. In our no-frills, six-person couchette for the nine-hour journey, I’ll admit I struggled to get comfortable on my hard lower berth. I’m awoken by occasional loud rattling and crunching brakes in the dead of night, but it feels a small price to pay for a more responsible way to travel. May 15, 2024 Español Take Charge of Your Diabetes Medicines Key points It's important to take your diabetes medicines correctly to stay healthy. Use this guide to help you stay on track to take all of your diabetes medications as prescribed. Tips to manage your medicines Take all medicines as directed. Tell your pharmacist and your doctor if: You develop any new problems like nausea, diarrhea, itching, or a rash. You have any problems taking your medicines (including forgetting to take them). You have questions about your medicines. You have any changes in your diet or health. You are pregnant or breastfeeding. You have trouble paying for your medicines. Why your medicines matter Make a list of all your medicines for your pharmacist and doctor. This way, you won't have to remember them all. It can be helpful to keep a copy in your wallet just in case. A Ferrari 296 GTS is just one of the supercars guests drive during the tour. Huntermoss By Charlotte Vowden Published October 21, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Many gearheads can only dream of sitting behind the wheel of A-listers like the Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica or Ferrari 296 GTS— but, for some, this is just part of a multi-vehicle supercar experience. Hunter Moss’s six-day tours turn the humble road trip into a luxury tour, switching between Bentleys, Aston Martins and Porsches as you cruise through the Swiss Alps. Travelling across Zurich, Andermatt and a range of awe-inspiring Alpine lookout spots, this tour of the Swiss Alps highlights can be completely tailored to the individual. For die-hard drivers with cash to splash, it’s the ideal way to witness the mountain views. Days 1 & 2: Set the Scene—Zürich to Andermatt Switzerland is made for a driving holiday: smooth, beautifully maintained roads wind through some of the Alps’ most spectacular scenery, linking high passes, lakeside towns and mountain resorts. The appeal of this particular trip is being able to enjoy them in a succession of supercars, swapping cars as the route unfolds.
